scope: ProjectStore.removeResearchVersions(ofDestroyed:) / sweepResearchVersions — a destroyed Research item's derived files
statement: A Research item destroyed for good takes its derived files with it: Permanently Delete and Empty Trash remove, for the item's ids (a group's children too, never an id back in the manifest), this device's versions under .maugham/research-versions/<itemId>/ AND the item's note record (.maugham/research-notes/<itemId>.json) and table sidecar (.maugham/research-tables/<itemId>.json), and only those ids; an item in the Trash keeps all three (a restore needs them, and an item in the Trash counts as live to the sweep), and a restore brings its writer mark and sidecar back. The open-time orphan sweep removes an orphan's record and sidecar (neither in the manifest nor in the Trash) once the file's own modification date is older than TrashStore.expiry — these files carry no device, so the file's age rules where a version folder's newest own file does — and keeps a younger one, whose Trash entry may still be on its way from another Mac. Known edge: another device's record or sidecar for an item whose manifest add has not synced within TrashStore.expiry could be swept by the same age gate the versions use. The op log of a manuscript document is not touched (M3-TR-049). Removing them is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16 (#141 N7), not Denver's; RULING-23 permits destruction without requiring it.
intent: INTENTIONAL — the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's
reachability: LIVE — Trash ▸ Permanently Delete or Empty Trash on a Research note, card or table; the open of a project

scope: ProjectStore.deleteResearchItems / trashResearchItemCore — a Research row whose file is already gone
statement: A non-link Research row whose file is not on disk (deleted in Finder, say) can still be deleted: it is trashed as the ROW only (a manifest-only entry, carriesFile false), so a batch containing it completes as one gesture and ⌘⌥Z puts every row back as one, and restoring puts the row back unchanged. A batch of rows whose files are all missing, or one missing row alone, does the same. 'Missing' means only a true no-such-file error (NSFileReadNoSuchFileError, or POSIX ENOENT directly or beneath it) with no .<name>.icloud placeholder beside the path: a folder Maugham may not read, an unreachable volume or an iCloud placeholder takes the ordinary route, whose move fails and is reported with the row and file left and no entry or folder made. That a row whose file is gone is deleted as the row, and the gesture completes as one, is RULING-63's; that 'missing' means only a true no-such-file error (an iCloud placeholder is a file still coming down, tripwire 18) is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's
intent: INTENTIONAL — ruled 2026-11-16 (RULING-63); the meaning of 'missing' is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's
reachability: LIVE — the binder or Research pane's Delete on one or several rows when a file was removed outside Maugham; then ⌘⌥Z
known_gaps: A missing GROUP is read by its folder (`namesAMissingFile`) and trashed with its rows in the entry; no test pins that arm, and its restore drops, and names in the report's unreturned, children whose files are gone (the existing prune).

scope: ProjectStore.deleteResearchItems — a gesture that stops partway
statement: A batch delete that fails partway says what it did and keeps undo honest (RULING-63, RULING-52's route). A throw from the FIRST item rethrows that item's own error unchanged, saves nothing and leaves the armed undo as it was. A throw from a later item (or after a row was removed with no Trash entry) saves the manifest without the rows already taken, refreshes the Trash list, arms ⌘⌥Z with exactly the entries that landed (labelled by the one title, or 'N items'; cleared when none landed, as M3-TR-036) and throws ProjectStoreError.deletedInPart(trashed:removed:failed:underlying:), whose sentence counts only what ⌘⌥Z can put back and names a row removed with no entry apart: “Moved 2 to the Trash (“A”, “B”), then “C” could not be deleted: <reason>. ⌘⌥Z puts the 2 back.” (“puts it back.” for one; “Moved 1 to the Trash (“A”) and removed “B”, then …”; “Removed “B”, then …” with no ⌘⌥Z clause when nothing is undoable; the underlying error's trailing full stop is dropped). If that manifest save itself throws, the error is manifestUnwritable carrying the save's reason and that sentence, with ⌘⌥Z already armed. A refusal asked of every item before any is trashed (M3-TR-066) is all or nothing: nothing is partial there. That the gesture stops, saves what landed, arms undo for it and names both halves is RULING-63's; the sentence's wording, the 'N items' label and the arm-or-clear rule are the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's
intent: INTENTIONAL — ruled 2026-11-16 (RULING-63); the sentence and the undo rule are the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's
reachability: LIVE — multi-select delete in the Research pane when one file is locked or unmovable partway through

scope: ProjectStore.restoreTrashEntry / restoreLastDeletion — a restore never makes a second row with an id the tree holds
statement: Restoring a manuscript or Research entry any of whose ids (a group's children too) is already in the tree it would return to is refused with TrashStore.TrashError.alreadyInProject(title:) — “X” is already in the project; nothing was restored. — before anything moves: the entry keeps its file and its place in the Trash and the tree is unchanged, and once the clashing row is gone the same entry restores once. ⌘⌥Z reads every entry of the gesture through its restore route and asks the same question of each (against the tree and against the gesture's earlier entries) before any entry moves, so a clash on the second of three restores nothing and leaves ⌘⌥Z armed. That an id clash is refused rather than inserted as a duplicate row is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's; that the gesture then comes back whole or not at all is RULING-40's
intent: INTENTIONAL — the refusal is the coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-16, not Denver's; whole-or-nothing is RULING-40's
